title: Repentance and Healing
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Repentance and healing teaches that restoration includes honest confession, turning from sin, receiving grace, and walking in truth. Biblical healing does not avoid repentance where sin is present, and repentance does not deny the need for mercy and care.
summary: Repentance and healing teaches that restoration includes honest confession, turning from sin, receiving grace, and walking in truth. Biblical healing does not avoid repentance where sin is present, and repentance does not deny the need for mercy and care.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls sinners to repentance and heals what sin has broken. Through Him, believers receive forgiveness, cleansing, and grace to walk in newness of life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Healing and repentance belong together when sin is involved. Scripture does not offer restoration by denial, blame-shifting, or hiding. It calls people into the light before God.

Repentance includes sorrow for sin, confession, turning from evil, and returning to God. It is not merely feeling bad or fearing consequences. It seeks mercy and a changed direction.

Healing also requires grace. People do not heal by crushing themselves with shame. God forgives, cleanses, restores joy, and helps His people walk in truth.

Some wounds are not the result of the sufferer’s sin, and those wounds require compassion rather than blame. Wisdom must distinguish between sin to confess and harm to grieve.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people want healing while refusing repentance. Others repent but remain trapped in shame as though God cannot cleanse them. Scripture speaks to both needs.

This doctrine helps ministry stay truthful and gentle. It calls sin what it is, offers grace where Christ gives it, and avoids blaming the wounded for harm done against them.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess sin honestly where God exposes it, and receive forgiveness through Christ. Do not hide, excuse, or despair. Seek wise help for wounds, walk in truth, and let repentance become a doorway to grace-shaped restoration.
